issue: Does a state-law drug offense count as a 'controlled substance offense' under U.S.S.G. § 4B1.2(b) only if it matches the federal definition of a controlled substance offense?

sides.position: A state drug offense can qualify as a 'controlled substance offense' under § 4B1.2(b) without being measured against the federal definition (the excerpt quotes only a truncated fragment of Lewis, so this is inferred from the opinion's description of the split).
cases: United States v. Lewis, 58 F.4th 764 (3d Cir. 2023)

sides.position: A state-law drug offense must be compared to the federal definition to qualify as a 'controlled substance offense' under § 4B1.2(b). The majority side (seven circuits) is described only as a count, and the excerpts do not name them.
cases: United States v. Chaney, No. 23-30454 (5th Cir. 2026)

quote: Indeed, as the government pointed out in its initial brief, there is a current 7–3 circuit split over whether to define state-law “controlled substance” offenses in § 4B1.2(b) by reference to the federal definition.
cite: United States v. Chaney, No. 23-30454 (5th Cir. 2026)
